title: Choose Clipvault's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Manila File. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Manila File
options.lineage: Indian government file folders: manila stock, pasted label slips, rubber-stamp ink
options.thesis: Your papers kept the way a clerk keeps them: in a file with a label, stamped when something moves.
options.viewport: A manila rail beside a crisp white working list; on the right the open item with a COPIED stamp on the number you just copied.
options.risk: Manila drifts into warm-cream nostalgia unless the working surfaces stay crisp white.

raised.raise: Stamp blue is reserved for the one thing you just did (copied, pinned), never for decoration.
Numbers sit in fixed cells, so an Aadhaar or PAN reads one character at a time.
Every item is identified from its edge by a label slip: kind and time left, in condensed caps.

options.label: The Comb-Box Form
options.lineage: Indian bank and passport application forms
options.thesis: Every number is set one character per box, like the form you are about to fill.
options.viewport: A pale form-green shell, square comb boxes carrying the open ID number.
options.risk: The most literal reading of this product, so most runs in this category would land here.

options.label: Streaming Wall
options.thesis: Screenshots and documents as tiles: the focused one grows, the rest dim.
options.viewport: Rows of screenshots and documents; focus grows one tile and dims the rest.
options.case: Holds product clarity for images and files, but history is mostly text, so it wins only that corner.
options.risk: A dark tile wall makes plain text history feel like a media library.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.case: Fuses poorly: handwritten ballpoint on a working list is a costume, not a tool.
options.kept: Every item is identified from its edge by a label.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.case: Fuses poorly: unlabeled colour codes defeat plain words for non-technical friends.
options.kept: Only the active item is decoded to full colour.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.case: Fuses poorly: poster-scale pixels fight a dense list and reduce readability.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.case: Fuses poorly: a map's terrain ground carries nothing a clipboard has.
options.kept: One reserved colour marks only the active layer.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.case: Fuses poorly: a flip-board costume turns a working list into an instrument.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A neutral three-pane clipboard manager with one blue accent, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, list and preview in Windows-neutral greys.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other clipboard managers by design.
